 (BY SHRI AMIT SETH - DEPUTY ADVOCATE GENERAL)
 This petition coming on for admission this day, the Cour  following:
 ORDER
The petitioner claims to be a public spirited person.
That he is an agriculturist and is a social worker.
He is an RTI worker also.
2. The instant petition is filed challenging the action of the State in proposing to construct the Patrakhokar Water Tank No.2 upstream of the river Umra Nalla situated near Village Patrakhokar.
3. The primary contention of the petitioner is that there already exists the Saroth reservoir which was constructed in the year 2004.
That notwithstanding the same, the State are committing an error in building this water tank which has been proposed by them.
Hence, he pleads for a direction to the respondents to stop the construction of the said dam.
4. On hearing learned counsels, we do not find any merit in this petition.
The very basis of the claim of the petitioner is not supported by any material.
It is only his mere contention.

Even though the existing Saroth reservoir is capable of holding water as mentioned, the question of the State putting up another water tank in order to deny water to the other villagers is not substantiated by any material.
The presumption is that the water tank and the scheme has been proposed in order to ensure that greater number of villagers benefit out of the available water.
There cannot be a scheme which denies water to one section of the Society while granting water to another section of the Society.
Therefore, the very basis on which the petition is filed is not supported by any evidence or material on record.
It would appear to be a mere apprehension of the petitioner.

Furthermore, the petitioner himself has stated that subsequent to he coming to know of the scheme being promoted by the State he has filed an application under Section 15 of the Right to Fair Compensation in Transparency and Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Transparency and Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, if at all he has filed such an application, it is for the concerned authority to decide the same in a manner known to law.

Under these circumstances, when none of the contentions of the petitioner are justified through any material and the same would appear only to be an imagination by the petitioner, we do not find any ground to entertain this petition.
5. The writ petition is accordingly disposed off.
(RAVI MALIMATH)
